[2326] XXV 286 CHILEAN AIR FORCE Book of the National Defense of Chile 2017 CHAPTER CHILEAN AIR FORCE The Chilean Air Force (FACH) was created in

[2327] Its creation was a product of the development that national aeronautics had achieved in previous years and the State's need for an independent military organization dedicated to dominating the air dimension

[2328] Thanks to decades of effort, the FACH currently has a significant strategic dimension and has served as the basis for the development of the various components of the national aerospace system

[2329] Vision To be a modern, integral and cohesive institution, with a defense capacity in line with the strategic needs and reality of the country, and recognized and valued by citizens in its role of service to the community, participatory and contributing to national development and territorial integrity

[2330] Mission The Mission of the Chilean Air Force is to defend the Republic of Chile through the control and use of airspace for its own benefit, participate in the surface battle and support its own and friendly forces, with the purpose of contributing to the achievement of the strategic objectives that the Defense Policy sets for the Armed Forces

[2331] Strategic institutional development The modernization process of the Chilean Air Force is aimed at generating a modern and powerful force

[2332] To maintain institutional potential, it is necessary to define institutional development planning based on three axes—Strength, Human Resources, and Management—which were defined to concentrate efforts and project the desired progress for the institution

[2333] Likewise, the aforementioned institutional development is manifested in three domains in which aerospace power is employed: airspace, cyberspace, and outer space

[2334] XXV CHILEAN AIR FORCE Book of the National Defense of Chile 2017 CHAPTER The foregoing translates into solutions and activities that, on the path of the institutional centenary, can respond in a congruent manner and in an integrated and cohesive way to the strategic needs of the National Defense, with useful, participatory and cooperative responses, in a way that allows projecting the Institution as a significant and versatile force at all times, circumstances and moments, in accordance with the requirements of the State

[2335] From the provisions of the Air Force “Centenary” Development Plan, two major objectives emerge in the area of technological projection: to incorporate cutting-edge technology and generate a critical mass that allows obtaining the maximum benefit from it, and to actively participate in the development of technologies together with universities and companies

[2336] In terms of technological innovation, it is necessary to modernize and eventually replace air and ground equipment from time to time, as well as train personnel

[2337] For this reason, the replacement of combat aircraft, transport aircraft, helicopters, UAVs, sensors, anti-aircraft artillery systems, and satellites must consider, on the one hand, the completion of their life cycles, staggering them over the years, and, on the other hand, the advantage that a modern weapons system provides by granting a high degree of operational availability

[2338] XXV 288 CHILEAN AIR FORCE Book of the National Defense of Chile 2017 CHAPTER Considering both the current situation and the fulfillment of the mission and the strategic vision of the Air Force, the Centennial Plan establishes the following objectives: a) Axis of the Force Configure the current force and support structure of the Institution, so that it is framed within the strategic requirements of the National Defense, the mission, the permanent functions, the whole and the institutional organization

[2339] Strategic Objective of Force 1 To have a force structure consistent with the new political and strategic realities, budgetary realities and government guidelines

[2340] • Strategic Objective of Force 2: To have weapons systems equipped with operational, technological, multipurpose, interoperable capabilities, operated by trained and instructed crews

[2341] • Strategic Objective of Force 3 To have, on a subsidiary basis, the capabilities to support the community in the event of natural disasters or links with isolated areas, within the current legal regulatory framework

[2342] Likewise, contribute to the projection of the State on the Chilean Antarctic Territory

[2343] • Strategic Objective of Force 4: Develop capabilities that act as multiplying factors in the use of aerospace power, enabling its sustainability and maximum exploitation, especially in the areas of cyber defense, electronic warfare, command and control systems, remote sensing, telecommunications, geoinformation, aerospace medicine, and the national aerospace industry

[2344] • Strategic Objective of Force 5: To enhance the contribution of institutional capabilities to the National Aeronautical System through the continuous development of space capabilities and by promoting the integration and synergy of the resources that comprise it

[2345] XXV CHILEAN AIR FORCE Chilean National Defense Book 2017 CHAPTER b) Human Resources Axis To enhance and obtain competencies in accordance with the capabilities, structure and performance required by the institutional mission, providing the individual with education, training and multidimensional support with due recognition and compensation for the contributions made to the Institution. • Human Resources Strategic Objective 1 To increase the number of Permanent Officers and Personnel (PCP), within the framework of the plant law, budgets and needs to effectively operate weapons systems, support systems and the organizational structure. • Human Resources Strategic Objective 2 To define educational and training curricular processes to train professionals with a clear sense of the military career of the Aviation Officer and Non-commissioned Officer; In addition, they must acquire the skills to manage the organizational and force structures that the Institution needs to fulfill its mission, considering education regarding the knowledge of Human Rights

[2346] The above includes the training of personnel on an extra-institutional basis

[2347] • Strategic Objective of Human Resources 3 Promote an attitude of proactive response to changes to face new scenarios

[2348] • Strategic Objective of Human Resources 4 Facilitate the family and personal management of Air Force members, related to their well-being

[2349] Management Axis Have an Integrated Institutional Management System, with strategic, operational and tactical prospective capacity, to operate in own, joint and combined environments in complex, dynamic and highly resolutive situations, both in times of peace, crisis or external conflict, as well as in the face of catastrophes, including scenario modeling and automated solution proposals in real time. • Strategic Management Objective 1 Strengthen the organizational structure in order to make it more efficient, produce synergy and avoid redundancies, integrating it with other joint extra-institutional organizational structures, in a way that ensures its coherence with the institutional strategy. • Strategic Management Objective 2 Implement an institutional tool that enables, in real time, control and management in all institutional processes, and that is equipped with an Institutional Statistical System, Uniform Databases, Costs and Multidimensional Data Modeling

[2350] • Strategic Management Objective 3 Optimize the Institution's administrative processes, making them faster and more profitable from a cost/efficiency point of view, with the purpose of improving timeliness, responsiveness and effectiveness

[2351] • Strategic Management Objective 4 Streamline regulations and standards to strengthen the doctrinal aspects of the Institution

[2352] XXV CHILEAN AIR FORCE Book of the National Defense of Chile 2017 CHAPTER Chart No. 39 ORGANIC OF THE CHILEAN AIR FORCE COMMAND IN CHIEF GENERAL SECRETARIAT GENERAL INSPECTORATE GENERAL AUDIT GENERAL DIRECTORATE

[2353] OF CIVIL AERONAUTICS GENERAL STAFF LOGISTICS COMMAND PERSONNEL COMMAND COMBAT COMMAND The Chilean Air Force has a functional organization, which is composed of the organizations listed in the following chart: Source: Chilean Air Force In order to fulfill its mission, the Air Force has a structure made up of the types of organizations defined according to the latest modification of Regulation Series “A”, No. 1, Organic and Functioning of the Air Force: a) Commander-in-Chief The highest institutional command is exercised by an officer with the rank of Air General and with the position of Commander-in-Chief of the Chilean Air Force, who is responsible for the senior leadership of the Institution and its administrative management

[2354] b) Advisory and management bodies The General Staff of the Air Force, together with the Inspectorate, Audit and the General Secretariat are the main working bodies of the Commander-in-Chief, whose mission is to advise him in the strategic planning and control of the Institution, in order to satisfy the demands of air activities in peacetime, wartime or crisis situations. international

[2355] Likewise, the Chief of the General Staff acts as the Military Aeronautical Authority

[2356] Operational Units or Forces • Major Operational Unit The Combat Command is the Major Operational Unit that reports directly to the Commander-in-Chief of the Air Force. Its mission is to prepare and train the institution's force structure, with the goal of achieving the level of operational readiness required by strategic planning. Subsidiarily, it collaborates in governmental and community support tasks, as directed by higher levels, with the purpose of contributing to national development

[2357] Operational Units They are represented by five Air Brigades, whose jurisdictions cover the entire national territory, both continental and insular and Antarctic

[2358] Air Brigades are operational units that exercise command over assigned tactical units within a geographic area

[2359] To this end, they have air and ground resources to achieve and maintain a level of operational readiness in line with institutional planning

[2360] Each of them is commanded by a General Officer who reports directly to the Commander of the Combat Command

[2361] Each Air Brigade has aviation groups, anti-aircraft defense groups, and telecommunications and computer groups

[2362] That is to say, the Institution's Air Power is materialized in these units

[2363] XXV CHILEAN AIR FORCE Chilean National Defense Book 2017 CHAPTER Chart No. 40 DEPLOYMENT OF AIR BRIGADES IQUIQUE I AIR BRIGADE V AIR BRIGADE II AIR BRIGADE III AIR BRIGADE IV AIR BRIGADE ANTOFAGASTA SANTIAGO PUERTO MONTT PUNTA ARENAS Source: Ministry of National Defense XXV 294 CHILEAN AIR FORCE Chilean National Defense Book 2017 CHAPTER d) Support units • Logistics Command It is an executive body that reports directly to the Commander-in-Chief of the Air Force, whose mission is to obtain, provide, maintain and develop the material, technological and logistical information resources to satisfy the needs derived from operational and development planning and those generated by institutional activities

[2364] Personnel Command It is an executive body that reports directly to the Commander-in-Chief of the Air Force, whose mission is to carry out the superior administration of the "Personnel" function in the areas of human resources, education, health, social welfare and air reserve, with the purpose of comprehensively developing the human resources of the Institution in support of the mission of the Chilean Air Force

[2365] Aerofotogrammetric Service (SAF)78 It is a service dependent on the Commander-in-Chief of the Air Force, which carries out its tasks through the Combat Command

[2366] The main function of the SAF, in addition to meeting the needs for aerial photogrammetry and remote sensing-based images and information, is to provide the official aeronautical cartography of the State and the plans that complement it

[2367] The functions of the SAF were established in Law No. 15,284, which created this Service

[2368] • General Directorate of Civil Aeronautics (DGAC) It is an agency dependent on the Commander-in-Chief of the Chilean Air Force, through which the State regulates and supervises air activity, both national and international, that takes place within the airspace controlled by our country

[2369] It also controls the air activities carried out by national airlines abroad

[2370] Since 1930, the DGAC has provided assistance and protection to air navigation through the gradual and constant application of cutting-edge technology

[2371] This has enabled it to create the conditions for the proper development of aeronautical activity, within a framework of speed, safety, and efficiency

[2372] The role of the SAF in the Air Force's contribution to national development is described in greater detail in Chapter XXVI

[2373] The role of the DGAC in the Air Force's contribution to national development is described in greater detail in Chapter XXVI

[2374] CHAPTER XXV CHILEAN AIR FORCE 25.5 Mission Areas The Mission Areas indicated below concentrate the tasks that the Institution must carry out in each of them: a) Defense In this Mission Area, the capabilities of the Air Force allow it to carry out tasks related to the development of national Air Power, the readiness of its means, the positive control of national space and the control of airspace assigned by international conventions, cooperation for deterrence, contribution to the management of an international crisis situation, strategic air transport and participation in military operations

[2375] International Cooperation In this Mission Area, the tasks carried out by the Air Force are related to its participation in peacekeeping missions and other international cooperation operations - according to the State's definitions in this regard -, its participation in combined exercises, its participation in humanitarian support missions and in the rescue of compatriots in danger from areas under conflict abroad, as provided by the political level

[2376] The Air Force's contribution in this Mission Area includes disaster prevention, response, and recovery tasks; security air activities; SAR operations; and contributing to national connectivity in various emergency situations

[2377] d) Contribution to National Development and State Action The contribution of the Chilean Air Force to national development and state action is realized through tasks of territorial integration, participation in the country's industrial and technological development, promotion of Chile's aerospace interests, and environmental protection at all Air Force bases and installations, including those located in Antarctica. e) Security and Territorial Interests In this Mission Area, the Air Force contributes to providing security and public order during States of Constitutional Exception, particularly during States of Catastrophe, as well as at polling places during electoral events

[2378] It also contributes to the national presence in Antarctica

[2379] PART EIGHT CONTRIBUTIONS OF DEFENSE TO DEVELOPMENT CHAPTER XXVI

[2380] THE DEFENSE SECTOR IN THE COUNTRY'S DEVELOPMENT CHAPTER XXVII

[2381] The Defense Industry Apart from their characteristic and primary missions, the military institutions of National Defense can carry out tasks in other Mission Areas, thanks to their multipurpose capabilities

[2382] Some of these tasks are specifically contributive to the country's development, and the Armed Forces carry them out within the framework of the Constitution and laws, and the definitions, decisions, and policies adopted or formulated by the Ministry of National Defense for such purposes

[2383] In this way, the Defense Ministry takes on tasks, for example, in the event of catastrophes, to help prevent or anticipate them, and, above all, in the subsequent reconstruction phase

[2384] It also provides support to local communities in isolated and remote areas and contributes to the unity of the national territory by facilitating connections by sea and air, or by opening land routes through the Military Labor Corps

[2385] It also carries out ongoing environmental protection work and seeks to adapt to changing climatic conditions and their effects

[2386] Likewise, Defense is an important source of human capital development and makes a direct contribution to the country's scientific and technological development

[2387] In these latter areas in particular, the Army Factories and Workshops (FAMAE), the Navy Shipyards and Workshops (ASMAR), and the National Aeronautics Company (ENAER), whether on their own or in partnership with other public or private companies, not only contribute to the military capacity of the Armed Forces, but are also a contributing factor to the country's growth in its productive and technological development

[2388] This is supported by the high level of specificity and added value of these National Defense companies

[2389] THE DEFENSE SECTOR IN THE COUNTRY'S DEVELOPMENT Chilean National Defense Book 2017. Chile is changing and State agencies must adapt to such transformations

[2390] For National Defense this means building a comprehensive vision of its role

[2391] Without overlooking the functions inherent to any defense system, it is intended to contribute to the national effort to address the challenges associated with sustainable development and the effects of natural phenomena that occur frequently in the country

[2392] To fully realize the defense sector's contribution to development, national defense institutions need capabilities that allow them to execute both strictly military tasks and those they might perform in other capacities: for example, response to earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions, forest fires, floods, and other natural or man-made disasters; search and rescue operations; and activities in the Antarctic

[2393] This is a modern and integrative approach to serving the Nation, both in times of peace and conflict, and considers policy formulation, plan development, and the fulfillment of tasks in the corresponding mission areas of National Defense

[2394] Social Responsibility Policy Various policies aimed at areas of activity related to the country's development in which National Defense plays a relevant contributory role are addressed in detail in several chapters of this Book

[2395] This section presents one of them, the application of which is transversal to the contributions that the sector makes to development

[2396] The initiatives and actions defined by the National Defense institutions within the framework of this policy contribute to sustainable development in social, economic, and environmental matters, as well as to strengthening social cohesion and promoting high standards of organizational management

[2397] In addition, National Defense promotes citizen participation and active interaction with society

[2398] Since the entry into force of Law 20,424, the Organic Statute of the Ministry of National Defense, the organization of this State portfolio includes the incorporation of tasks and functions associated with social responsibility and development collaboration

[2399] In this context, a variety of actions are being carried out with the institutions of the Armed Forces, as well as with other dependent agencies that are part of the Ministry of National Defense

[2400] Of particular importance are the activities carried out by the Armed Forces in coordination with other state agencies to develop public regulations related to the study, conservation, and control of natural resources, natural disaster management, climate and oceanographic studies, and the fight against pollution

[2401] In order to contribute to national unity and cohesion, the Armed Forces provide direct support to citizens, consisting of a series of activities that, together, promote the strengthening of trust, civic friendship, civic responsibility, the cultivation of patriotic spirit, and the preservation of the nation's historical and cultural heritage

[2402] These activities take on a particularly significant meaning when the Armed Forces come to support the community in emergencies and natural disasters

[2403] In matters of sustainability, institutions carry out environmental protection activities

[2404] Social and economic development is realized through actions that support isolated human settlements, scientific research, and the effective exercise of our sovereignty

[2405] In the area of organizational management, policies, programs, instruments, and actions related to management modernization, transparency in the use of resources, good labor practices, and support for staff and their families are considered

[2406] Defense planning and contribution to development In the new planning process, these two areas group together all the tasks that the military institutions of National Defense carry out on a recurring basis, based on the well-being of the population affected by catastrophes that are now aggravated by the effects of global warming and climate change, or in response to social needs such as health or the integration of local communities living in isolated or extreme areas of the country

[2407] To realize its contribution to the country's development, the Defense sector has considered, in the new methodological design of capabilities-based planning, the possibility of conceiving them for use in a broad spectrum of missions. These missions, without losing sight of the main purpose of National Defense to ensure the country's peace and external security, include aspects of contributing to development and civil protection in the event of emergencies

[2408] Hence, among the five National Defense Mission Areas defined for planning purposes, two have been identified that are directly related to the Defense sector's contribution to the country's development: National Emergency and Civil Protection, and Contribution to National Development and State Action

[2409] Armed Forces and their contribution to development New challenges make it necessary to diversify the technical and professional skills of the military institutions of National Defense, which have the capacity to deploy throughout the territory with direct effects on the lives of people, regions, and their economies

[2410] This requires armed forces with multipurpose capabilities that allow them to operate in areas defined by their specialties, which, in turn, are integrated into specific areas of society

[2411] In addition, the branches of the Armed Forces have service organizations, as well as scientific and technological organizations, that perform tasks that are strictly institutional in nature, but that can also benefit research, innovation, and development in areas such as energy, space, and the environment

[2412] These institutions are: a) Military Geographic Institute (IGM) This is the Army unit that acts as the official, technical and permanent service of the State in all matters related to the cartography of the national territory in different scales and formats

[2413] The institution is used as a base for Geographic Information Systems (GIS) applications for civil and military purposes, and has the capacity to generate digital terrain models

[2414] Among the services it provides, which have been added over its eighty years of existence, are Geography, Cartography, Geodesy, Photogrammetry, and Image Processing, among others

[2415] It also plays a role in public outreach by promoting scientific meetings and geographic conferences, in addition to representing Chile before national and international organizations related to Earth sciences

[2416] Military Labor Corps (CMT) is an Army unit designed to actively participate not only in the execution of road works that generate connectivity and communication within Chilean territory, such as roads and bridges, but also in the construction of housing (for example, after an earthquake) and irrigation works

[2417] The CMT has five subdepartments throughout the country (Arica, Santiago, Puerto Montt, Coyhaique, and Punta Arenas) and its goal is to connect the entire national territory by land, which is expected to be completed in the next decade

[2418] Over the past 40 years, the CMT has built more than 2,200 km of access roads, 4,000 meters of runways, 883 permanent bridges, two ramps, and a pier in nine regions

[2419] Geographically, the body's presence extends from Visviri, in the far north, to Tierra del Fuego, integrating 80 local communities into the national community and generating connectivity for a territory equivalent to Switzerland, Austria, Belgium, and Portugal combined

[2420] Hydrographic and Oceanographic Service of the Navy (SHOA) It is a unit of the Navy that provides support to institutional operations and makes a broad contribution to the development of the country

[2421] In addition to working to ensure the safety of lake, river, and maritime navigation, it performs all the tasks required for the development of nautical cartography, including aerial photogrammetry applied to nautical charts

[2422] It is the technical body that controls and disseminates the official time throughout the national territory, in addition to being responsible for the operation, maintenance, and operation of the National Tsunami Warning System (SNAM

[2423] In this regard, since 2010, a significant investment has been made in infrastructure, technology, and personnel to optimize tsunami prevention and warning

[2424] Among the main innovations is the installation of a new network of 40 tidal stations from Arica to Antarctica, which significantly increased the frequency of data reception

[2425] Additionally, since April 2013, it has a sensor network, positioned between 186 and 139 NM of coastline, from Iquique to Constitución, which is part of the global monitoring network and provides real-time data regarding alerts of possible sea level changes affecting Chile's coasts

[2426] The Air Force Aerophotogrammetric Service (SAF) is the State's technical and governing unit in the aerospace field, at the forefront of the use and operation of remote sensors for data capture, and the processing and dissemination of images and geospatial information useful for analysis and decision-making, both for Defense and for other areas of national development

[2427] In addition to meeting the needs of the Chilean Air Force in the areas of remote sensing, aerial photogrammetry, and related techniques, the SAF must meet national needs in its areas of expertise, carrying out specialized work for all state administration entities and private individuals, with the aim of contributing to aviation safety, defense, and national development

[2428] It is interesting to note that, as a public service, it provides services to entities such as mining, agricultural, and other companies that require cartographic precision

[2429] The service has the capacity to directly receive images from various international satellites, which complement the information received from the national satellite FASat-Charlie

[2430] For these purposes, the institution has geographers, pilots, photographers, cartographers, surveyors, photogrammetrists, and other professionals on the ground throughout the country

[2431] e) Space Operations Group (GCE) The Air Force Space Operations Group is the organization that the State has to control the positioning and tracking of its own spacecraft, as well as to schedule the acquisition of satellite images and receive their corresponding data on the ground

[2432] The GOE monitors the current and future position of the satellite currently in use (FASAT-Charlie), carries out the position corrections that are instructed to the satellite, and finally receives the raw product

[2433] The GOE works together with the Aerophotogrammetric Service, providing it with the data obtained to transform it into information usable by military and civilian users

[2434] This organization incorporates human resources from all defense institutions, both military and civilian, forming a critical mass of space specialists

[2435] e) General Directorate of Civil Aeronautics (DGAC

[2436] The DGAC fulfills its mission by providing the following strategic products: "Airport Services", "Air Navigation Services", "Operational Safety Services" and "Meteorological Services

[2437] These strategic products are delivered through the extensive national airport network, comprised of 342 airports and airfields spread from Arica to Antarctica, including those on our island territory

[2438] Aeronautical activity is carried out within the security framework provided by the General Directorate of Civil Aeronautics, providing the necessary means and services to generate connectivity within the territory

[2439] This is a fundamental condition, considering the complex geography of our country

[2440] Hence, it should be considered a social good, as it allows for immediate assistance and relief to those in need, providing closeness and protection to the national community

[2441] The air transport system allows the State to connect with the globalized world, which constitutes an important contribution to the country's growth

[2442] This contribution has been a factor in the country's tourism growth, facilitating access to our natural attractions, which in many cases are only possible by air

[2443] The Chilean Meteorological Directorate (DMC), which reports organically to the DGAC, provides aeronautical meteorology, general meteorology, and climatology services, which impact the State's human security efforts, particularly in climate-related emergencies

[2444] It is the organization that provides weather alerts to the National Emergency Office of the Ministry of the Interior (ONEMI), provides information to the Civil Protection Committee, and provides updated information for decision-making by the Emergency Operations Committees, in accordance with the National Civil Protection Plan

[2445] Likewise, the DMC contributes to the country's economic activity by providing the necessary climatological information for water management forecasting and, in general, decision-making in the agricultural sector

[2446] This concept includes the various Scientific and Technological Study and Research Centers dependent on Defense institutions, whose purpose is to contribute to increasing knowledge in their respective areas of expertise

[2447] To this end, they form networks for the exchange of experiences through cooperation agreements with other national and foreign entities

[2448] Institutional activities contributing to development a) Action in response to disasters The military institutions of National Defense have had an active participation in national disasters and emergencies

[2449] Evidence from the field work carried out by the Armed Forces shows that the deployment of military personnel in such situations has been decisive and necessary

[2450] As an illustration, we can recall what happened in the Chillán earthquake or the Valdivia earthquake and the subsequent work to clear Lake Riñihue

[2451] Recent examples include the Tarapacá earthquake, the Tocopilla earthquake, the Chaitén volcano eruption, and the earthquake and tsunami of February

[2452] Following the 2010 catastrophes, which are among the most significant in Chile's seismological history, other disasters affected the country, such as the earthquake in the Tarapacá and Antofagasta regions in 2014; the floods in the Antofagasta, Atacama, and Coquimbo regions in 2015; and the earthquake in Coquimbo in

[2453] The great Valparaíso fire in 2014 and the 2017 wildfires in the O'Higgins, Maule, and Biobío regions deserve special mention due to their magnitude and the devastation they caused

[2454] In all these events, the military presence in mitigation and reconstruction tasks was decisive, especially due to the concentration of personnel, resources, and action protocols

[2455] Environmental Protection The Armed Forces carry out various actions that contribute to environmental protection, which are a contribution to the sustainable development of the country and to the efforts made in recent years by the State in this area

[2456] Directly related to the environment, climate change is having significant effects on various sectors of the country, including defense

[2457] The increase in the frequency and intensity of natural disasters is an example of this phenomenon

[2458] The Army, Navy, and Air Force have long had environmental policies and carried out environmental work

[2459] But, in addition to these tasks, the Ministry of National Defense is developing a Climate Change Policy that will allow this variable to be included in the work of Defense and its institutions in a coordinated manner. This, added to the actions already carried out by the Armed Forces, will allow an organic contribution to national efforts regarding climate change

[2460] An analysis of climate change as a phenomenon in the international context is found in Chapter V and a description of the action of National Defense in relation to climate change is included in Chapter XII

[2461] Regarding environmental matters, the military institutions of the National Defense have promoted the following initiatives: Army This institution has been developing its environmental policy in two areas: an internal one, which seeks to adapt its work to the State's environmental guidelines; and an external one, in which the Institution collaborates on the preservation of ecosystems in conjunction with other State entities

[2462] At the internal level, the Army made the following decisions during 2016: - It updated its 2012 environmental policy by publishing the directive document "Army Environmental Commitment," which provides general guidelines for channeling institutional efforts regarding the environment, sets objectives, and guides the implementation of initiatives in "institutional environmental sustainability

[2463] It updated its Environmental Management System, managed by the Logistics Directorate, to fulfill the tasks of maintenance, protection, preservation, and conservation of the institutional environmental heritage

[2464] It published its Environmental Regulations, which establish the framework for action on environmental matters and incorporate the State's advances and regulations regarding the environment

[2465] Through a vision focused on the development of garrison activities, the Army seeks to improve the quality of life of military personnel, their families, and the community, for which it participates in various plans and programs: Restoration of tree and shrub species, and implementation of afforestation and reforestation plans

[2466] • Implementation of energy, water, and non-conventional renewable energy measures. • Waste management, which includes the development of initiatives to address the quantity and variety of hazardous and non-hazardous waste generated within the units

[2467] On the external front, the Army's activities are focused on strengthening strategic alliances and promoting environmental education

[2468] All of this, based on the cooperation of public and private entities leading to sustainability

[2469] • Navy The Chilean Navy is aware of the effects that climate change may have on the operations and tasks to be carried out by the Institution

[2470] For this reason, the Navy Climate Change Committee was created to, among other things, advise sector authorities when required and develop subsidiary planning, along with programs and action plans, in accordance with the guidelines provided by the Ministry of National Defense in its sectoral policy on this issue

[2471] Furthermore, the Navy's Environmental Policy addresses environmental protection through actions carried out both within and outside the Institution, with two distinct areas: - Internal Naval and Maritime Area: This covers all members of the Institution, including naval units and divisions

[2472] The main objective is to prevent, reduce, and control environmental pollution, in order to achieve a quality of life compatible with the protection of human health and ecosystems, consistent with the Institution's activities and actions

[2473] To achieve this goal, the sources and effects of environmental pollution resulting from institutional activities had to be identified and evaluated

[2474] External Maritime Scope: This includes the public sphere of action under the jurisdiction of the General Directorate of Maritime Territory and Merchant Marine (DGTM and MM), in its role as the National Maritime Authority and representative of the State of Chile in maritime environmental matters

[2475] Among the objectives of this area of action are the protection of the environment from pollution by hydrocarbons, toxic waste, and other harmful substances, with the aim of maintaining a global environmental balance

[2476] This action ensures the quality of life and the protection of the aquatic environment and its natural resources

[2477] Air Force The Air Force has defined environmental guidelines since 2012, which were updated in the new institutional environmental policy of

[2478] This policy demonstrates a commitment to environmental preservation, incorporating sustainability as a permanent challenge in fulfilling its mission

[2479] It aims to consolidate environmental management at the respective levels of the Institution's organizational structure, based on the following principles: - Preventively, preserve the environment by promoting actions to identify and control activities that could affect it; reactively, mitigate potential damage that institutional activities could cause

[2480] Comply with and monitor current environmental legislation and regulations, as well as international agreements and treaties signed by our country that are applicable to our institutional situation, through the development of internal regulations

[2481] Finally, promote environmental awareness through staff training

[2482] The National Ocean Policy is discussed in more detail in Chapter IV and the Strategic Plan for Biological Diversity is addressed in Chapter XIV

[2483] Both instruments provide a framework for the contribution of National Defense in the area of biodiversity

[2484] Among the initiatives that the Air Force has undertaken in relation to environmental management, particularly through the General Directorate of Aeronautics (DGAC), the following stand out: - Promoting the concept of "Green Airports" so that air terminals have standards designed to ensure that airport facilities have the least possible impact on the environment in which they are located

[2485] Promote the environmental sustainability of the Chilean Aerospace System development process by establishing specific environmental policies (including the implementation of an Environmental Management System

[2486] Certify six airports/aerodromes under the international standard ISO 14001 and implement the same standard at five aerodromes, all of which are part of the national primary network

[2487] In addition, a clean production agreement (CPA) was signed at Mataveri Airport on Easter Island

[2488] These environmental management systems comply with regulations on liquid and solid waste (including hazardous waste), as well as spill control

[2489] As a result of the implementation of the second runway project for the Arturo Merino Benítez Airport in Santiago, a series of measures were implemented to protect the airport's natural environment and minimize the impacts generated by its operation

[2490] The wildlife risk mitigation and assessment study within the Arturo Merino Benítez Airport Avian Hazard Area (APA) was also updated to achieve a balance between aircraft operations and the surrounding natural environment

[2491] Protecting Biodiversity The National Defense institutions, including the Ministry of Defense, have contributed to the State's efforts in this area, both in relation to the country's land and inland waters, as well as its marine and coastal areas

[2492] The Strategic Plan for Biological Diversity and the National Ocean Policy point in that direction

[2493] Particularly regarding the protection of the oceans, an issue that is part of said policy, the creation of the following marine parks stands out: XXVI 308 THE DEFENSE SECTOR IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE COUNTRY National Defense Book of Chile 2017 CHAPTER Chart No. 41 MOTU MOTIRO HIVA MARINE PARK • Multiple Use Coastal Protected Area "Mar de Juan Fernández" (Supreme Decree No. 10 of 2016), with an area of 11,027.66 km

[2494] Motu Motiro Hiva Marine Park: Created by Supreme Decree No. 235 of the Ministry of the Environment, dated December 4, 2010, with an area of 150,000 km2, in order to preserve the marine ecosystems around Easter Island

[2495] Likewise, those associated with the seamounts that constitute part of the continental shelf of the Salas y Gómez Range and the components of the aquatic biota present in this protected area, as a way of contributing to the conservation of national and global biodiversity

[2496] • Nazca Desventuradas Marine Park: By Supreme Decree No. 5 of the Ministry of the Environment, dated March 14, 2016, the “Nazca Desventuradas” Marine Park was created, with an area of 300,000 km2 in the Exclusive Economic Zone of the San Félix Islands, thus contributing to the conservation of a marine area of significant biodiversity and the largest marine park in America

[2497] Currently, the decreed Marine Protected Areas (MPA) cover a total area of 463,233.63 km2, equivalent to 13.6% of the MPA extension that the country has

[2498] This represents an important contribution to fulfilling Chile's international commitments

[2499] Furthermore, the Ministry of National Defense has a National Coastal Use Policy aimed at planning and managing coastal and maritime spaces, geared toward sustainable development

[2500] This is a forum for participation by all stakeholders along the coastline, thus contributing to the development of environmental protection areas in line with the interests of each region of the country

[2501] Additionally, the defense sector participates in the National Committee of Protected Areas (CNAP), created on February 3, 2014, by Exempt Resolution number 83 of the Ministry of the Environment

[2502] He has also participated in the development and creation of the National Biodiversity Strategy 2016-2030 and the National Wetlands Strategy

[2503] For its part, the Chilean Army has participated in various initiatives for the protection and conservation of biodiversity, such as: the project to create a system of protected areas in the San Pedro River Valley in the Los Ríos Region; the conservation of the ruddy-backed gull in the Magallanes Region; and the protection plan for the lesser tern in the Arica and Parinacota Region

[2504] Likewise, the incorporation of sustainable management into the administration of land and environmental management of the Chilean Antarctic Territory, in compliance with the Antarctic Treaty and the Madrid Protocol

[2505] XXVI THE DEFENSE SECTOR IN THE COUNTRY'S DEVELOPMENT Book of National Defense of Chile 2017 CHAPTER XXVII 312 THE NATIONAL DEFENSE INDUSTRY Book of National Defense of Chile 2017 CHAPTER THE NATIONAL DEFENSE INDUSTRY The companies that make up the defense industry in Chile are state-owned, private, or mixed

[2506] State-owned enterprises are managed according to the principles of economic public order, particularly with regard to integrity and transparency; that is, they are subject to government oversight and the oversight of the Comptroller General of the Republic. The state-owned defense industry is closely tied to the existence of the branches of the Armed Forces, and its essential functions are to meet the maintenance and supply requirements of each of the military institutions with war material

[2507] These companies have achieved a significant level of industrial and technological development, which has enabled them to meet the missions and objectives set out in their respective special laws

[2508] Its logistical support capabilities allow for relative technological independence, a relevant aspect considering the challenges and technological requirements posed by the weapons systems acquired by the Armed Forces institutions

[2509] State-owned defense companies, specifically the Army Factories and Workshops (FAMAE), the Navy Shipyards and Workshops (ASMAR), and the National Aeronautics Company (ENAER), communicate with the government through the Undersecretariat of National Defense, without prejudice to the organizational units established by law

[2510] In recent years, the Ministry of National Defense has been working on a proposal to strengthen the corporate governance of state-owned defense companies, taking into account best practices established by the OECD

[2511] This effort is aimed at providing greater stability to the board members, prioritizing their skills, stability, and continuity

[2512] a) Army Factories and Workshops (FAMAE) It is a Public Law Corporation that has legal personality, autonomous administration and its own assets, whose purpose is to manufacture, recover and market war elements to satisfy in the broadest and possible way the needs of National Defense, being able to manufacture, repair and market all kinds of machinery, tools and industrial articles, as well as provide services related to each of the aforementioned tasks

[2513] Its industrial and technical capacity contributes efficiently and effectively to National Defense, meeting the demands of its main client, the Chilean Army, through the maintenance of armored material, production, co-production, recovery, development and marketing of weapons systems and war elements, as well as through the provision of all those elements or services associated with said systems: the associated military infrastructure, innovation, and development and information technologies required to provide efficient support to the force

[2514] In this area, it serves as the main supplier of weapons systems to the Chilean Army, integrating different technologies and origins, providing confidence and security in their operation, and generating technology transfers with national participation in maintaining the material throughout its life cycle through an efficient comprehensive maintenance service

[2515] Through its subsidiaries—Arcomet SA and Servicios y Soluciones Tecnológicas (S2T)—it integrates into the defense industry, meeting the demands of the Army and Armed Forces and Law Enforcement institutions, as well as other domestic and foreign clients, by identifying technical, operational, and logistical solutions based on its engineering and industrial strengths

[2516] b) Shipyards and Naval Workshops (ASMAR

[2517] The Chilean Navy Shipyards and Workshops (ASMAR), an autonomous state-owned enterprise, has the primary function of repairing, careening, and constructing Chilean Navy units. With its surplus capacity and without affecting its primary function, it can undertake the repair, careening, and construction of domestic and foreign vessels

[2518] Basically, ASMAR concentrates its activities in four areas: • Services: It primarily focuses on the calibration of instruments in the electrical, dimensional, pressure, time and frequency areas

[2519] • Shipbuilding: Among the projects developed and implemented are logistics support vessels, auxiliary vessels, and general service vessels

[2520] To date, it has built 112 ships and naval vessels

[2521] Maintenance and Repair of Naval Units: Offers comprehensive service to all types of vessels, in the areas of structures, electricity, electronics, optics, optronics, diesel engines, metallurgy, machine tools, and carpentry

[2522] • Recovery, Modernization, and Conversion of Units: Among the most significant recovery projects are the conversion and modernization work carried out on destroyers, frigates, missile boats, submarines, auxiliary units, and foreign naval combat units

[2523] Due to its activities, ASMAR is strategically located and has plants in Valparaíso, Talcahuano, and Punta Arenas

[2524] In addition, it owns a 90% stake in the company “Systems Engineering and Functional Development Company Ltda”

[2525] SISDEF), dedicated to systems integration and the development of command, control, communications and computer systems, and the Ibero-American Society of Naval Repairs (SOCIBER), whose business is the repair and careening of ships

[2526] These companies were created to complement ASMAR's activities in their respective fields, in partnership with internationally renowned European companies

[2527] National Aeronautics Company (ENAER). The National Aeronautics Company of Chile was created in 1984 to encourage the development of the national industry in the repair of aircraft, engines, and components, with a strategic focus on supporting the operations of the Chilean Air Force at a time of many restrictions on access to foreign markets

[2528] Since its inception, it has provided aircraft maintenance services, transformation, and modernization of combat, transport, and helicopter aircraft. It has also built the T-35 "Pillan" primary military training aircraft for the Air Force (FACH), which it successfully marketed in Spain and six Latin American countries. It also co-manufactured the C-101 advanced training and light attack aircraft

[2529] In addition, it incorporated the business segment for manufacturing parts, components, and subassemblies, which it sold primarily to EMBRAER, Airbus Military, Marcel Dassault, and Lockheed Martin, among others

[2530] At the end of 2013, the aerostructures manufacturing contracts with EMBRAER and Airbus Military were concluded, preserving the knowhow, which has been used to support aircraft maintenance and recovery

[2531] The company was organically restructured, with an emphasis on aircraft, engine, and component maintenance, primarily with the Chilean Air Force

[2532] This meant changing its business model, signing framework contracts, and deploying its maintenance teams to major air bases across the country, expanding its range of services

[2533] Additionally, the provision of maintenance services to other National Defense institutions was increased, and the commercial aircraft maintenance business was resumed

[2534] In parallel, production and administrative processes have been optimized by applying, among others, the Public Enterprise System's corporate governance best practice guidelines, supported by updated and efficient information systems

[2535] This vision for the future also involves strengthening and developing human capital and ensuring economic and financial stability, applying concepts of Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development that consider stakeholders and their environment, in order to efficiently execute ENAER's operations, primarily benefiting the aeronautical system and National Defense

[2536] Strategic Importance of the National Defense Industry FAMAE, ASMAR and ENAER contribute to Defense by meeting the maximum possible technological demands of the Chilean Armed Forces

[2537] They have also promoted the development of science and technology in the military field with applications in the civilian sphere

[2538] They have also contributed to innovation activities in technological niches of interest to the country

[2539] They are defined as strategic because they allow the country to have a certain degree of autonomy in the face of maintenance, adaptation, or manufacturing needs for certain types of military equipment

[2540] Regarding mixed and private defense companies, their main focus is the development, repair, and maintenance for the improvement and complementation of military institutions' weapons systems

[2541] The areas that have shown the greatest development are electronics and software, particularly those applied to sensors, fire control, electronic warfare systems, unmanned systems, and command and control systems

[2542] Furthermore, given the importance of companies in the sector, the Ministry of Defense supports national events such as FIDAE and EXPONAVAL, as they are mechanisms for promoting the products and services of defense companies, especially with benefits for various small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs

[2543] Events like these are ideal venues for networking with international companies and showcasing national capabilities and products. They are also a way to contact potential clients and identify partnership options for national or international defense projects

[2544] Development of the National Defense Industry One of the challenges facing the Ministry of Defense in technological matters is to formulate an industrial policy that stimulates the involvement of industry in the development of National Defense capabilities

[2545] This industrial policy should seek a balance between the country's strategic defense objectives and the necessary self-sustaining capacity of state-owned defense companies, so that they can adequately fulfill their legal obligations

[2546] Ensuring the usability and sustainability of important technologies and fostering the development of the national defense industry are initiatives that would allow for the desired degree of autonomy in making strategic decisions without limitations imposed by a lack of technology or the will of external suppliers

[2547] From this perspective, the Ministry of Defense is promoting initiatives such as the following: Strengthening the competitiveness of the state defense industry: The state defense industry must be prepared to participate in national and international procurement tenders

[2548] It is necessary to create legal and administrative mechanisms to facilitate these companies' provision of their products and services not only to the Armed Forces (which must continue to be their primary reason for existence), but also in other markets to ensure their operational continuity and allow them to generate economic opportunities that, if properly exploited, can be a substantial source of income for the country

[2549] Improve NATO cataloging of defense supplies: Cataloging is a set of activities and procedures that allow for the identification and classification of defense articles and supplies among NATO countries

[2550] The Ministry of Defense has managed the adoption process for this series of standards

[2551] • Build research and development capacity: It is essential to promote research and development in state-owned defense companies to provide effective support for the systems and equipment incorporated into military institutions throughout their entire life cycle

[2552] This would reduce dependence on foreign suppliers in areas that can be defined as strategic for the country

[2553] • Promote National and International Cooperation Agreements: In addition to existing agreements, there is a need to promote the signing of other defense cooperation agreements that generate synergies with public and private, national and international entities, while also taking advantage of the opportunities these agreements offer in terms of research and innovation, and for the co-financing of common projects of interest to the sector

[2554] Build research, innovation, and development capacity: It is essential to promote initiatives in the aforementioned areas within state-owned defense companies

[2555] Spatial Continuity Project (Spatial policy is framed; this project is addressed in Chapter IV

[2556] Among the most innovative initiatives contributing to the country's development in which the National Defense participates is the activity related to outer space

[2557] The project corresponds to the successor spacecraft to FASat-Charlie, both belonging to the Earth Observation Satellite System (EOSS), which consists of a remote sensing optical system, composed of a space segment and a ground segment

[2558] The space segment is basically the satellite, equipped with a state-of-the-art sensor for acquiring high-resolution images of the Earth, and the ground segment is where the images are produced and the operation of the space segment is controlled

[2559] This project aims to obtain, process, and deliver information to support government decision-making in emergency and disaster situations using satellite imagery

[2560] Additionally, as a subsidiary benefit, it aims to foster national and international cooperation by contributing to the country's technological development and providing information for academic, scientific, and industrial activities, which contribute to strengthening Chile's strategic stature

[2561] Some of the applications for which satellite observation products can be used to benefit society, after processing, include precision agriculture, flood control and prevention, volcanic eruption monitoring, forest fire control, mapping, urban growth planning, security and defense, among others

[2562] This new strategic capability presents significant improvements over FASat-Charlie, as its conceptualization addresses the needs of both the Defense and Joint Chiefs of Staff, as well as those of public agencies, the scientific community, and civil society in general. This capability provides a strong component of subsidiary benefit for the country's development, optimizing distribution mechanisms to broaden the range of users more quickly and efficiently

[2563] The current satellite in operation was defined under a theoretical useful life of 5 years, which was completed in

[2564] Given the need for its replacement, the technical evaluation process for the space continuity project, based on the methodology defined in the regulatory framework of the Ministry of National Defense, concluded in 2017 and is now ready for implementation
